script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 16. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Damage happens.  Things break—objects, relationships, trust.  But broken doesn't mean over.

Effective apologies have parts: recognition ('I see what I did'), responsibility ('It was my fault'), remorse ('I feel bad about hurting you'), and repair ('Here's what I'll do differently'). Skip any part and the apology feels hollow. Japanese kintsugi repairs broken pottery with gold, making the cracks beautiful.  It doesn't pretend damage didn't happen—it incorporates it.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Broken things can become stronger at the break points.  Repair adds rather than merely restores.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Repair Initiative - Fix One Thing.

Here's your activity: Is there a relationship with unaddressed damage? A conversation you've been avoiding? A wrong you haven't made right? Take one step toward repair today—acknowledge, apologize, or reconnect. Repair is a skill that improves with practice. This helps you practice relationship repair.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about making things right can be applied to repair initiative - fix one thing. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
